title: Testing Whether Deliberative Alignment Training Reduces Scheming on Open Models

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: tests whether a known mitigation (deliberative alignment) generalizes from frontier to open models. A positive result provides an accessible intervention; a negative result narrows the applicability of the technique.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires LoRA fine-tuning, constructing a deliberative alignment dataset, and designing scheming evaluation scenarios. This is advanced ML work beyond beginner CS students even with guidance.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Involves dataset creation, fine-tuning, and before/after evaluation on scheming scenarios. While LoRA is efficient, the end-to-end pipeline (dataset + training + evaluation) is sustained effort for a 30-hour project.

novelty.reasoning: While deliberative alignment has been studied on frontier closed models (o3, o4-mini), no work has tested this technique on open-weight models. The transfer question is genuinely open and novel, though the technique itself is established.

evidence: Apollo Research & OpenAI (2025) 'Stress Testing Deliberative Alignment for Anti-Scheming Training' tested deliberative alignment on o3 and o4-mini (frontier closed models), achieving ~30x reduction in covert actions.
The deliberative alignment technique has only been tested on OpenAI frontier models, not on open-weight models like Llama or Mistral.
No published work found applying deliberative alignment training to open-weight models to reduce scheming behavior.
